neighbours.label: buying everyday goods: ' buy' / '买' in a household shopping context (groceries, soap, shoes), not corporate acquisition
fire: On Saturday morning my mother walks to the market to buy fish and fresh fruit.
We ran out of rice, so I went down to the corner shop to buy some more.
妈妈每天早上都去菜市场买菜，然后回家做饭。
He stopped at the pharmacy on his way home to buy soap and toothpaste.
With my first pay cheque I could finally buy new shoes and clothes for the children.
奶奶让我去楼下的小店买一瓶酱油。
Every week they drive to the supermarket to buy groceries and other household things.
The children saved their pocket money to buy sweets and toys at the fair.
quiet: On Saturday morning my mother walks to the river to feed the ducks and swans.
We ran out of time, so I went down to the corner office to ask for more.
妈妈每天早上都去公园散步，然后回家做饭。
He stopped at the pharmacy on his way home to ask about the opening hours.
With my first pay cheque I could finally visit my parents and thank them for everything.
奶奶让我去楼下的小店找一下邻居。
The investment fund agreed to acquire the airline's shares for three billion dollars.
The children saved their pocket money and counted the coins every night before bed.

notes: In probes 'buy a rival firm' scored 0.17 and 'grocery shopping' without a buy verb 0.02. The - pole fires before 'article(s)/item(s)/goods' as a noun for merchandise.
